task.title: Position-aware paths_rw_split sinks + variable-level sanitization
task.body: Task 112's `paths_rw_split` invariant lists `File.cp!`/`cp_r!`/`cp`/`cp_r`/`rename` in `@file_writer_fns` position-unaware, so `File.cp!(Paths.priv(...), target)` trips it even though the writer target is unrelated. Two band-aids were applied (rewriting `File.cp!` as write+read in `pipeline.ex`, broadening `@file_reader_fns`); both mask-bleed into a theoretical false negative. Proper fix: (a) position-aware sinks distinguishing write-position args from read-position args, likely via a registry keyed on `{function, arity, write_arg_indices}`; (b) variable-level sanitization so Reach sanitizes the specific variable passing through a reader, not every node on the chop — likely needs a Reach-side change. Once either lands: narrow `@file_reader_fns` back to content readers, restore `File.cp!` in `pipeline.ex`, delete both TODO blocks. Discovered 2026-04-24 during staged-review of the paths_rw_split sanitizer-broadening change.

task.title: Retrofit Pattern B timestamp writers to accept an :extracted_at opt
task.body: `mix ccxt_extract.determinism_check` currently strips volatile timestamp keys before comparison because Pattern B writers stamp `DateTime.utc_now()` at write time. The strip-keys list is a workaround — the gate can't catch a regression landing inside a stamped-timestamp envelope. Scope: thread an optional `:extracted_at` (and siblings) through the Pattern B aggregate writers — `AggregateWriter` and per-extractor envelope builders — so the determinism harness (or a `--frozen-clock` flag) can pass a fixed timestamp; default stays wall-clock. Then `determinism_check` passes a frozen clock instead of stripping keys. Discovered 2026-05-14 during Task 114 (Phase 3b).

task.title: Track indirect signature placement via request-like object construction
task.body: htx (and likely others) build `const request = {..., Signature: signature}` then `url += '?' + this.urlencode(request)`. The placement is genuinely `query` with key `Signature`, but Task 65 derivation only tracks direct `query = ...` / `headers['K'] = ...` / `body = this.json({...})` assignments. Add an object-level propagation step: when an ObjectExpression with a sig-referencing property is bound to a variable, follow the variable into subsequent `url += '?' + this.urlencode(<var>)` / `body = this.urlencode(<var>)` statements and attribute the placement. Discovered during Task 65 (htx.private ships `signature_placement: null` until this lands). Distinct from the retired LFS Task 113 (corpus untracking) — same number in legacy ROADMAP, resolved separately.

task.title: Multi-hop body alias resolution in pre_sign_transforms body-encoding detector
task.body: Task 68's `PreSignTransforms.body_reached_by_crypto?/2` resolves a single alias hop (catches okx `auth += body`, bitfinex `const auth = ... + body`). It does NOT catch multi-hop chains like `payload = body; auth += payload; this.hmac(auth, ...)` or fixed-point fan-in. Scope: extend the tracer to a bounded fixed-point — visit each crypto-arg identifier, expand its 1-hop set, recurse, with a max-depth guard (3–4) and a visited-set for cycles. Honest non-convergence leaves the field empty. Don't conflate with Task 66h (canonical_string concat-chain resolution) — they share the alias-hop primitive but target different consumer fields. task.title: mix ccxt_extract.prune — evict out-of-scope local state
task.body: `AggregateWriter.merge/2` is intentionally additive so scoped runs accumulate — which means `priv/discoveries/` per-exchange subdirs and envelope aggregates drift out of sync with the declared scope (e.g. `priv/output/` held 23 priority files while `describe/` held 107). Everything except `class_hierarchy.json` is gitignored, so the safety rail never fires. Scope: a new mix task accepting the same `--tier*/--all/--exchange ID` / `Paths.out(...)` plumbing, computing the in-scope ID set via `Tiers.members_for_tier/1` + class_hierarchy, deleting out-of-scope per-exchange files in all `priv/discoveries/<subdir>/` (plus matching `priv/output/<id>.json`), then re-aggregating every envelope file from only the surviving in-scope files — never touch `class_hierarchy.json`. Honor `:priv_write_override`. `--dry-run` by default, `--force` to actually delete. Success: post-run ID sets in `priv/discoveries/describe/`, `priv/output/`, and envelope `by_exchange_id` stamps all match. Discovered 2026-04-20 from a scope-drift report.

Replace both with a scope-aware helper that reads `_manifest.json`'s `tier_scope`, resolves it via `Tiers.members_for_tier/1` + `class_hierarchy.json`, and only skips when the target exchange is honestly out of scope. Drop the `:tier3_corpus` exclusion and `@tag` once the helper lands. Discovered 2026-04-20 during Task 117 code review.

task.title: Extract unified-method descriptors from CCXT TS — TS signature + JSDoc overlay
task.body: CCXT's unified methods carry two complementary axes: (a) the TS method signature — ordered `.value.params` with name, TS type, optional flag, default value, plus return type — the structural source of truth; (b) a leading JSDoc block adding per-param prose, `@throws {ErrorClass}` entries, `@returns` shape — the semantic overlay. Both halves matter; don't ship JSDoc alone. Extract both via an OXC pass over method definitions and emit a unified-method descriptor per method so each downstream client maps it to its own arg-shape convention — do NOT encode any single consumer's arg-shape in the descriptor. The TS-signature half is mechanical; the JSDoc half is the unknown — verify whether OXC surfaces JSDoc through `leadingComments`, a program-level comments array, or needs a second pass; QuickBEAM over the TS source is the fallback. Also emit `descriptor.source` — the byte-for-byte method body slice via OXC `.start`/`.end` offsets (provenance `raw`, just the method body, no normalization) so the descriptor becomes self-verifying. Provenance: both halves `raw`. Partial descriptors are honest (missing JSDoc → `description: null`, `errors: null` + `unresolved_reason`). Emission shape left to the implementer. Discovered 2026-04-21 during a descripex surface audit. ([Opus] model-hint marker from the legacy ROADMAP dropped — retired-era convention.)

task.title: Extract JsonIO.write_json!/2,3 + a deterministic_write contract invariant
task.body: Commit f3ea824 (Task 114) spread the deterministic-emit pattern `File.write!(path, Jason.encode!(AstNormalize.to_encodable(x), pretty: true))` across 15 executable write sites in `lib/` (`exchanges`, `aggregate_writer`, `describe` ×2, `signing_fixtures` ×2, `discovery_writer`, `load_markets` ×2, `base_methods`, `public_exchanges`, `pipeline` ×2, `error_class_hierarchy`, `mix/tasks/ccxt_extract.setup`). `CcxtExtract.JsonIO` already owns the read side (`read_json/1,!`). Scope: add `JsonIO.write_json!/2,3` wrapping `to_encodable` + `Jason.encode!` + `File.write!`, migrate the 15 sites, and add a `deterministic_write` corpus-level invariant to `mix ccxt_extract.contract_test` (mirroring `paths_rw_split`'s `Reach.Project.taint_analysis/2` shape) that fails when a `lib/` write site emits JSON without routing through the helper — so the determinism-emit contract has a single enforcement point and a new write site can't silently break byte-determinism. Discovered 2026-05-14 by staged-review:audit-review on commit f3ea824 — Claude + Codex convergent: both independently resolved "file as ROADMAP follow-up" (good abstraction, but corpus-invariant-scale work, not an audit-commit splat). See `.audit/f3ea824-task-114-determinism-audit.md`.

task.title: Extend transaction_classification to non-unified raw broadcast endpoints
task.body: Task 73d shipped a name-only classifier over CCXT's unified-method namespace; consumers correctly cannot trust `on_chain == false` (or absence) as a safety gate because non-unified raw paths bypass the convention. Coverage gap: DEX flows exposing blockchain transactions via helpers like `signL1Action` / `signEIP712`, implicit-API paths like `public_post_sendtx` / `sendTxBatch`, and sign-method bodies that construct a signed-payload-then-broadcast shape. Approach: an OXC pass over sign-method and exchange-method bodies looking for (a) known signed-payload helpers, (b) web3 / EIP-712 typed-data builders, (c) `sendTx` / `sendTxBatch` patterns, (d) DEX-specific signing imports (`@noble/curves`, `ethers`, `starknet`). task.title: OXC-side extractor for sign-method-constructed User-Agent and runtime header mutations
task.body: Captures two QuickBEAM blind spots Task 73b can't reach because the values aren't in resolved `describe()`: (1) `bigone.ts` constructs `User-Agent` inside sign() as `'ccxt/' + this.id + '-' + this.version`; (2) `okx.ts` mutates `this.headers` at runtime via `setSandboxMode(true)` to inject `x-simulated-trading: 1`. Both need an OXC pass over sign-method bodies to detect (a) string-concat assignments to a `headers['User-Agent']` LHS, (b) `setSandboxMode`-equivalent runtime mutations on `this.headers`. Output would extend `runtime.request_headers` (or a sibling) with sign-time / sandbox-time variants. Score is low — affects 2 known exchanges, low consumer impact, high OXC complexity. File but defer until a priority consumer surfaces a concrete need. Discovered 2026-05-07 during Task 73b.

task.body:
Make v4 the default published schema. Flip every `schema_target` default from 3 to 4
across pipeline / validate / update mix tasks, and swap `@schema_version` /
`@schema_filename` in `schema.ex` to the v4 values (drop the `-pre` suffix: `4.0.0-pre`
-> `4.0.0`).

The load-bearing change is `validation.ex`. The `check_*_roundtrip` functions key on v3
output paths (`runtime.describe`, `structure.class_info`, `structure.sign_method`, ...)
and are currently silently disabled under v4 by the
`effective_schema_only = schema_only or schema_target == 4` bypass. Rewrite each
round-trip function to its v4 path (`raw.describe`, `raw.class_info`, `auth.sign_method`,
... — the reshape table is in SCHEMA.md) and remove the bypass so round-trip coverage
runs on every default run. `Schema.build_exchange_v4/4` is the authoritative source for
each v4 path.

Do NOT delete v3 in this task — `build_exchange/4`, `exchange_v3.json`, and the
`--schema-target` flag stay reachable so the tree stays green and each commit is
reviewable. Deletion is Task 143.

freeze-gate / retention language), CLAUDE.md (the two `exchange_v3.json` factual refs in
the Architecture and Common-commands sections), CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md (Source-column
paths -> v4). Flip the `Task v4-adopt` row in `../ccxt_client/ROADMAP.md` to unblocked
per the cross-repo documentation invariant.

task.body:

behaviour changes, just complexity removal.

Delete: `priv/schema/exchange_v3.json`; the v3 builder `Schema.build_exchange/4`; the v3
validator `validate/1` + `validate!/1`; the v3 `@required_*` module attributes. Collapse

`@v3_to_v4_pointer_prefixes` table, and the `--schema-target` flag plus

tasks. In `provenance.ex`, promote the `_v4` pointer attributes/functions to canonical
and drop the v3 ones. Remove v3-only tests and the v3 round-trip functions; fold the
`schema_v4_emit` cached-test coverage into the baseline pipeline/schema tests.

Task v4-adopt is done first.
